balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Bajaj Auto Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Bajaj Auto Limited: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Bajaj Auto Limited: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Bajaj Auto Limited: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Bajaj Auto Limited: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Bajaj Auto Limited: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Bajaj Auto Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Bajaj Auto Limited: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Bajaj Auto Limited: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Bajaj Auto Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue

salesVolume.title: Total sales volume
salesVolume.content:
Sales volume is total units (two-wheelers plus commercial vehicles) sold in the period, domestic and export combined.

For Bajaj Auto Limited: Bajaj is a volume-and-mix business -- Revenue growth that outruns volume growth means price/mix (higher-value models, exports, spares) is doing the work, not units.

What to watch:

  • Volume growth versus Revenue growth -- a widening gap is price/mix, not demand
  • Seasonality: Q3 (festive season) is typically the strongest domestic quarter

volumeMix.title: Domestic vs export volume
volumeMix.content:
Units sold split between the domestic Indian market and export markets (Africa, Latin America, South Asia being the largest).

For Bajaj Auto Limited: exports have been the faster-growing half of the volume base and carry a different currency and competitive profile (Nigeria, Egypt and other African markets are a large share) than the domestic two-wheeler market dominated by commuter models. A rising export share raises FX and country-risk sensitivity. Only three quarters are disclosed in filings so far (Q1 FY2026, Q4 FY2026, Q1 FY2027) -- too short to call a trend, but the direction is visible.

What to watch:

  • Export share of total volume rising or falling
  • Which export markets are driving the swing (disclosed in management commentary, not this chart)

segmentVolume.title: Two-wheeler vs commercial vehicle volume
segmentVolume.content:
Units sold split between two-wheelers (motorcycles) and commercial vehicles (three-wheelers and small goods carriers).

For Bajaj Auto Limited: two-wheelers are the large base; commercial vehicles are the higher-margin, more cyclical segment tied to urban mobility and last-mile freight demand, and to CNG/EV substitution in the three-wheeler fleet. Only three quarters are disclosed so far (Q1 FY2026, Q4 FY2026, Q1 FY2027).

What to watch:

  • Commercial vehicle volume growth relative to two-wheelers -- it is the segment most exposed to EV/CNG three-wheeler competition
  • Whether CV's margin contribution (not shown here) keeps pace with its volume share

otherIncomeTax.title: Other income and cash tax rate
otherIncomeTax.content:
Other income is non-operating income, predominantly interest and dividends on Bajaj's large investment portfolio (the company holds a significant corpus of mutual funds and bonds alongside the vehicle business). Cash tax rate is cash taxes paid as a percentage of pre-tax profit.

For Bajaj Auto Limited: Other income is large enough (roughly 8-12% of EBITDA in most years) that it is not noise -- it is a real contributor to net income that depends on treasury returns, not the vehicle business, and the DCF's owner-FCF build backs most of it out as non-operating.

What to watch:

  • Other income rising faster than the investment corpus would imply (one-off gains)
  • Cash tax rate drifting from India's statutory corporate rate (~25.2% effective since the FY2020 rate cut)
